title: Flat towns with no visible hills
description: Flat towns with almost no hills visible around are usually in the central-eastern areas of Curaçao.

title: Unpaved roads
description: Random unpaved roads are seen more commonly in the western half of the island.

title: Western rural landscape
description: The western part of Curaçao is dominated by a dry, rural landscape with rolling hills and scattered developments connected by narrow roads.

title: Labadera rainy coast
description: This coastal area near Labadera has a very specific look: rainy coverage, very low vegetation, and a line of wind turbines visible.

title: Shete Boka national park
description: Shete Boka national park on the northern coast has a similar landscape to Labadera but with sunny coverage instead of rainy.

title: Northern mountains
description: Northern mountains with shrubby vegetation

title: Hills with rock walls
description:
Hills with rock walls are not very common, but if you see one you're most likely in the 
central-eastern part.

title: Big groups of palms
description: Big groups of palms (10+) can be found in Willemstad. They are quite rare in other areas.

title: Prickly pear cacti
description: Prickly pear cactus can be found far more commonly in the western part of the island.

title: White small flowers (northern mountains)
description: These white small flowers can be found only in the northern mountains of Curaçao.

title: Tiled roofs (especially red)
description: Houses with tiled roofs, especially red ones, are most commonly found in Willemstad. They can appear elsewhere but less commonly.

title: Multi storey houses
description: Multi storey houses are found mostly in Willemstad.

title: Residential buildings
description: Residential buildings (apartment blocks) can be found only in downtown Willemstad.

title: Non-residential buildings
description: Non-residential buildings (offices, commercial) can be found only in the Willemstad area. Less common outside downtown.

title: Dense development with narrow roads
description: Dense development with very narrow roads can be found pretty much only in downtown Willemstad.

title: White-red bollards
description: These white-red bollards are quite rare, but when visible they are almost always found in Willemstad.

title: Decorative street lamps
description: Decorative lamps can only be found in coastal downtown Willemstad.

title: Telecommunication masts on distant hills
description: Telecommunication masts placed on hills far away can be found only in the Willemstad area.

title: The Aloe Vera farmmm
description: The only aloe farm on the island. Recognizable by aloe growing everywhere.

title: Plantage Flor De Madeira
description: A distinctive palm plantation found in north-eastern Willemstad.

title: Stick stuck in camera lens (Grote Berg)
description: In the town of Grote Berg and on part of the road next to it, a stick is stuck in the Google camera lens.

title: Leaf stuck in camera lens (east of Jan Donker)
description: On a few roads east of Jan Donker, a leaf is stuck in the camera lens. The leaf can look different in different parts.

title: More exposed car front
description: On roads in eastern Seru Grandi (Willemstad) the front of the Google car is more exposed than usual.

title: Downtown Willemstad
description: The only place on the island that looks like a town. Characterized by numerous residential buildings, narrow streets, very dense development, and extremely common red tiled roofs. Includes Otrobanda, Scharloo, Punda, Pietermaai.

title: Steenrijk district
description: Steenrijk has many characteristic narrow roads with quite dense development (slightly less than downtown), lots of pastel-colored houses, and uses way less tiled roofs than the rest of Willemstad. Includes Marie Pampoen.

title: Parera district
description: Very distinct district of Willemstad with limited coverage, very sparse development. Lake Shottegat is almost always visible to the north.

title: Eastern Willemstad
description: Feels much warmer than the rest of Willemstad. Most coverage is very sunny and noticeably hilly. A unique hill is very often visible to the southwest, south, or southeast. Includes Montana, Seru Grandi, Cas Grandi.

title: North-Eastern Willemstad
description: Somewhat hilly with usually sunny coverage. Random big hills commonly visible in the distance. Full white houses are quite common. Includes Abrahamsz, Santa Catharina.

title: Central Willemstad
description:
There are no characteristic things about central Willemstad. 
It's a little bit hilly, and the coverage is sometimes sunny, sometimes cloudy  (but it feels a bit 
colder than east of Willemstad).

title: Northern Willemstad (flattest region)
description: The flattest region of Willemstad. Commonly cloudy, and the only part of Willemstad where you sometimes see rainy weather. Includes Brievengat, Jongbloed, Emmastad, and many more neighborhoods.

title: Western Willemstad
description: One of the most hilly parts of Willemstad. Weather is very often cloudy. A distinctive hill with 4 communication masts is very commonly visible. Includes Piscadera, Mundo Nobo, Domi, Charo, Wishi.

title: Sint Michiel
description: Mostly pretty flat with partly cloudy weather. Two distinctive hills are commonly visible to the south in the distance. Includes Jan Doret, Boka Sami.

title: Jan Thiel
description: Looks very rich, coast almost always visible to the south, lots of white houses with red roofs. Almost the only place where you can commonly see full white villas.

title: Grote Berg town
description: A rich, flat town where you can usually see the coast. Lots of houses with tiled roofs, very common villas and multi-storey houses. More dead-end streets than any other town. Also recognizable by the stick in camera.

title: Daniel
description: Very distinct town with unique, rich-looking pastel-colored houses with very intense red tiled roofs. Limited coverage.

title: Tera Kora
description: A very flat town that looks like Grote Berg but much poorer. The coast is often visible, with a wind turbine farm.

title: Sint Willibrordus
description: A small town with sparse development, surrounded by distinctive small flat-topped hills.

title: Jan Donker
description: A hilly town with probably the most sparse development on the island. Commonly has very red soil and small narrow roads.

title: Barber
description:
Barber is a pretty hilly town, with a pretty sparse development.  
There's literally nothing characteristic about this town. It just exists.

title: Soto
description:
It's a hilly town with a very sparse development. 
It's even less characteristic than Barber.

title: Jan Donker
description: A hilly town with probably the most sparse development on the island. Commonly has very red soil and small narrow roads.

title: Lagun
description: Very distinct town. Coast is visible from almost every spot to the west, and distinctive hills to the east. No other town looks like this.

title: Sabana Westpunt
description: A flat town on the coast surrounded by hills. Coast visible from many spots. Distinctive hills visible to the south or southeast.

title: Christoffel national park road
description: Located in the most mountainous region. A very narrow road with no road lines, large bushes, and a unique dark strip in the middle. Part of the road has rainy coverage.

title: Road to Watamula hole
description: Very distinct road with red soil, a bit wider than other rural roads, coast visible, very flat, lots of big prickly pear cacti, and very clear sky with almost no clouds.

title: The Lagun-Sabana road
description: One of the only bigger roads that is mostly isolated with no houses, poles, or civilization around. Surrounded by hills, usually no road lines, cracked pavement, very sunny. Random darker spots on pavement with a thin cracked line in the middle.

title: The Lagun-Sabana road
description: One of the only bigger roads that is mostly isolated with no houses, poles, or civilization around. Surrounded by hills, usually no road lines, cracked pavement, very sunny. Random darker spots on pavement with a thin cracked line in the middle.

title: Weg Naar Westpunt — cloudy part
description: This section has partly cloudy weather with the sun behind clouds. Pretty hilly with some houses along the road. Road lines are not visible or only faint outer lines. Usually has lamps on the sides.

title: Weg Naar Westpunt (flat part)
description: The flattest part of Weg Naar Westpunt with almost no hills visible. Sometimes coast visible to northeast. Random houses and ad signs on the sides.

title: Weg Naar Westpunt (prickly pear part 1)
description: Wilder section, more hilly and overgrown. Lots of prickly pear cacti on the sides. Single unbroken middle line. The only road outside towns with chevrons on the island.

title: Weg Naar Westpunt — prickly pear part 2
description: Similar to part 1 but more open, less wild, lower vegetation. Coast sometimes visible, lamps more common, and some random houses around.

title: Schottegatweg
description: The biggest road on the island: a four-to-six lane road going around Lake Shottegat. If you see a four-lane road, you're on this road. Weather is usually cloudy.

title: Tafelberg Road
description: Most distinctive clue is a unique sidewalk always visible on the right side. A distinctive hill is visible in the distance from most parts. The coastal section has a distinctive beige wall on the left.

title: Tafelberg Road
description: On the coastal part you can see this distinctive beige wall on the left side of the road.

title: Weg Naar Bullenbaai
description: A road surrounded by big hills with variable pavement quality. Weather is cloudy, which makes it very distinctive. Old rusty guardrails are common. Two lakes visible on the sides at one point.

title: Queen Juliana Bridge
description: Easily spotted by its yellow and blue guardrails and awesome view over Willemstad.

title: Sandals Royal resort
description: One of the weirdest places in Curaçao. Beige, extremely rich-looking buildings with an absurd amount of palms around.

title: Flamingos at Salt Lake Willibrordus
description: Flamingos can be seen on Salt Lake Willibrordus, east of Sint Willibrordus.
